candidates.review_text: I love the atmosphere of this place.  Even if you are just getting a quick coffee to go you are treated like a special guest.  I have tried several different sandwiches and salad and have thoroughly enjoyed each meal I ordered.  They are dog friendly in the take out area and give the dogs bacon if you allow it.

Ditto to everything all the 5 star reviews say, plus this: it's DOG FRIENDLY!

Seriously. You can go in. With your dog. 

I was waiting for a friend outside one day -- had my dog with me -- and one of the employees waved me right in, insisting they welcome dogs.

And they did! How very European.... 

Been back a few times with my pooch. Love this place.

The staff is friendly, the bagels and coffee are fresh, and those combine with atmosphere to make me feel very much at home. Another plus for this place is that it's also a pet friendly spot, Not that I would subject the other patrons to my pup for extended amounts of time. I appreciate that if I'm taking my dog on a long walk he can come in with me while I grab a quick drink and I don't have to leave him tied up outside in the cold. They're a bit of a walk from house but when me and my dog are on a mission B2 is usually a short stop I have to make.

The food, service and setting was perfect for a quick casual lunch at Washington Square.  We had beef and pork bulgogi salads and mango smoothly. The fact that it is pet friendly was a huge plus.  They even brought a bowl of water for him.

Great atmosphere. 
Super friendly staff. 
Dog friendly.
Cute outdoor seating lining the building.
Munchies in addition to great coffee.

LOVE.

I Love this place. The atmosphere is nice, relaxing and a good time. I found this place when my friend had his birthday there. The food can be a hit or miss sometimes but the service is amazing. Don't be afraid to say something (politely).  The staff are all nice, sociable, helpful and knowledgeable. 

They are Dog friendly which is a big plus. I have gone there twice with my little pup and several times before I got him. 

*However, Make sure you order your food specifically the way you like it or  a little under because they may over do it a little. The Tuna burger is wonderful- just sear it. Good place to have a burger, fries and a beer (or 2 ).

Great service, good food and dog friendly.  Cute interior bar and dining area.  We are outside under an umbrella with the dog.  Plenty of dog bowls.  Great beer and wine list.  We had salads and Philly steak sandwich.  Chicken lettuce wraps were good but hard to eat, as the lettuce didn't wrap around.  Nice street for people watching.

This place is awesome. Dog friendly so I'm allowed in. They have internet for my made-for-dogs laptop. And it's not too busy so I don't get overly excited and have an accident or start barking.

I do wish they had more egg-based dog food (eggs, I mean eggs) so I don't have unhealthy-for-dogs carb loaded bagel every morning. 

Other than that the ambiance is perfect and the people operating the coffee shop are fantastic.

Stopped by for brunch today with the bf and our dog and we were seated immediately outside. Their outdoor seating is very dog friendly and before we even ordered the staff had brought a water bowl and treats for our pup. He was very pleased and so were we. 

The bf ordered the $15 lunch special with the salad and the ahi tuna poke bowl. There wasn't abbot left, he loved it. I had the French toast which was a little unusual but very tasty! (Just not your typical French toast w/ syrup). 

Our server was very nice and checked on both us and our pup! 

The prices were great considering the poke bowl is normally more than $15.

The patio was great and it's always a plus being able to have our dog join us for brunch. He got a lot of attention from staff and other diners. 

This was our first visit but I'm excited to come back and try dinner.

We once got an order for delivery from the Plough and Stars during the winter that was brought to us by an outside delivery service. The food was soooo good, hearty and excellent comfort food for a snowy day inside. We have been dying to try it again but this time at the physical restaurant. The building is an historic corn exchange. It's stunning inside. A huge hearth with a fire, balcony with seating and long bar area. Supposedly they have live Irish music at times as well. We sat outside in the super comfy captains swivel chairs because we had the dog. They are the type of place that asks if they can bring your dog a bowl of water when you sit down. I had wings and my boyfriend had fish and chips and a drink from the bar. They have a separate menu for bar food and then also have a separate full meal type menu. Everything was solid, friendly staff, dog friendly, nice ambience, decent prices!

Great service, DOG FRIENDLY, stiff drinks, and good food.

The atmosphere is very chic, outdoor seating is comfortable and nice. The drink names are very quirky and fun I ordered the "Party by Myself" and "I want a Divorce" both were very good and I highly recommend getting a Divorce. The waiter even brought out a water bowl for our dog! I also ordered the fig flatbread which was Devine. I highly recommend this place. 

I will definitely come back

I always go back and forth with with place. The staff is always amazing and very friendly. I have always enjoyed the drinks, the food is 50/50 some days its amazing and other it seems very greasy. 
I will keep going back though, so i would recommend it!
and its dog friendly!!!!

They only have 4 tables for outside eating but our server was amazing and very nice the food was good and I recommend this place and give them your time they are trying to make it during these trying times. Oh and they are dog friendly which is always a plus with me! Nice local hangout spot.
We sat outside and the ambience is beautiful. Food and booze were equally good. Great wait staff. Restaurant is on a quiet street and outdoor seating is pet friendly.

Great service, I was hesitant on ordering one of the newer dishes (which I will not name for privacy!) on the menu but knowing me, I wouldn't give up a chance to try anything that piques my interest or if it's new! The server was so friendly yet felt my uneasiness ordering. After taste testing the new dish, I really... really... did try to finish it but had to stop after 2 bites because of how pungent the taste was. I even tried to cover up my dish or cut it up into smaller dishes to hide the fact that I didn't enjoy it as much as I thought I would, which my husband just laughed at me for. No surprise, the server noticed right away when collecting my dishes and laughed but graciously offered to not add it on the tab! Dont know about you, but I call that attentive service, worthy of coming back -- and not to mention, with our dog! We sat outdoor and they are pet friendly

Hubby and I had a delicious steak dinner today. Service was very good.  

While we were there, two women and a man came in. The one woman was holding a small Maltese dog. They were seated and served. 

I love dogs and I think dog friendly restaurants are fine provided they have outdoor seating.  I know of such a Longhorn in Florida. 

I don't believe this small dog was a service dog, but perhaps an emotional support dog. I don't know. 
I guess this bothers me because I think some people are taking advantage of the whole service dog thing. A service dog is trained to help the owner as necessary. 

I know anyone can purchase a vest for their dog that says service dog, but they may not really be a trained service dog. 

I think this behavior can only hurt the true service dogs.

Great food, drinks, ambience, and crowd! Dog friendly outdoor seating. Attentive wait staff. 

This is a neighborhood place that treats you like you have lived in that neighborhood all your life!

i love this place because the people who work there are nice.  i love the neighborhood.  i love the fact that they cater to the dog friendly neighborhood, they have dog leash hooks and water bowls available for the puppies.  the restrooms are always clean.  the swordfish special was amazing, as was the tuna... but i like my tuna seared so i had to send the "medium" one back, but they were all over it! i love the bread pudding desert, but i'm not a fan of nuts and oats so stay away from the crisps.  i don't know i really like their drink menu too, and there's just something about the place.

Made reservations and was able to be seated a bit earlier since we arrived before our reservation time. The place was packed and I could see/hear that they had a live band inside. 

They have indoor and outdoor seating and I could see that they had seating upstairs as well. 

Drinks: PGT Elixir and the Hot Tropic. The elixir was really good, had a sweet taste to it and wasn't to gingery. The hot tropic was a bit tart for me but I'm told it was good as well. 

Ordered the clam chowder and it wasn't the white creamy chowder I was expecting so I was kinda thrown off. The soup was okay but it did have a lot of crab meat inside which I pleased about. 

Dinner:  We shared the chicken sandwich, which we ordered with a side Cesar salad and fries. The fries were really good. The sandwich was ok, wasn't much real flavor. I bit into and didn't taste any flavor just a fried chicken sandwich w/a piece of lettuce and tomato. (Didn't finish)

I was turned off by the dog that was seated next to me. I understand restaurants being pet friendly (I guess) but you've forgotten about your paying human customers. Not everyone likes dogs, not everyone wants one seated next to them, some people have had traumatic interactions with dogs. Therefor I think it would be appropriate to ask a customer if they mind having a dog next to them or just have a completely separate area for animals and there owners. And the dog had an odor which really turned me off.

The food was fair. I have a service dog and they told me no dogs allowed. When I reiterated that my dog was a service animal the server disappeared and came back and asked for papers. I said there are no "papers" and he left again. From there another server came out and waited on us. This server was not engaging and was slow to respond to our requests. There was only one other customer in the restaurant most of the time we were there. I was disappointed.

Not a pet friendly restaurant. The only reason we choose to visit this very restaurant. Very disappointed, the guy who looks like the owner or the manager was not even friendly. Such a waste of a time going all the way there from our hotels.

Not dog friendly! We called ahead and asked specifically if they allow dogs/pets on their outdoor patio and we're told "yes of course! Outdoor seating is first come." Walked their and the hostesses asked if our dog was a service animal, we said no and they said they don't allow pets and that they were "jut reminded right now of the policy."

Alright...f**k this! 

Food's INCREDIBLE but the service is TERRIBLE!!!
Went there with a service dog who helps with seizures and blood sugar levels. Called ahead to see if: they are pet friendly, have outdoor dining and if it's heated. 
The heating wasn't really there and the server was straight up an a*****e!!! 
Absolutely no pleasantries and he tried to rush us out like we're untouchables! 

Dogs are better than humans, try to be BETTER. 

Not going back again EVER!!!

A real shame indeed. It had been since before the pandemic that I had gone to the Cafe. I've always enjoyed the food. However, this time we brought ourwas one of the most rudest person we ever encountered, chastised us for having a dog, and basically ruining our entire meal, that we had to leave without even finishing our food. Not at all dog friendly place!

Me, two friend and 2 companions(service dogs) walks into the premises and gets greeted by a distraught waitress who says no dogs allowed in the building, understandable because it is a good serving place, so we tell her they are service dogs are are legally allowed to be in here, she then listens to us and proceeds to  get her manager, who then comes out with the same distraught greeting and attitude (shaking his hand left and right and saying no dogs allowed, well good afternoon and welcome to you too). We tell him the same thing that they are service dogs and we have ID for them, he tries to give us an option of sitting outside which I appreciate but we want to dine inside because it's August, hot af outside and it's about to pour rain. He then goes somewhere to check something but we were already bummed by their attitude, I can't rate their food since we didn't even get greeted lol. I'm not mad at them but I'm mad at their approach. We went to Fuel instead, one block down the street and healthier. They even gave the doggos water. Bless.

outdoor seating but no dogs allowed? interesting. however we stood in their restaurant area with no service while we looked for something that was dog friendly. this is not very independent of you, "independence" beer garden.

So, I walked in here hoping for a great selection and good service. However, I bought my little yorkie mix, who is a service animal, specifically an emotional support animal for children. Upon entering, I was told I couldn't bring my dog in. First of all, this is Fishtown, which is extremely dog friendly. Second of all, I told the guy he was a service animal and he said and I quote, "we don't allow all service animals, for example, emotional support animals". This isn't just illegal, it is absurd. Walked out upset and annoyed and definitely didn't order anything. The menu wasn't anything to write home about anyhow.

Chayya was dog friendly. Now only service dogs? Won't be going there anymore even for my coffee in that case. Being dog friendly on the ave was their biggest asset. This is super disappointing. Two thumbs down.

Update! Now I just won't come in because of the rude and unprofessional response from flannel. See ya never!

In a beautiful city full of Mexican options-this one is just so so. 

The food is pretty good-I gotta give them the fact that they have decent tacos. But that's always the most basic item and something nobody should be able to fumble on.

Drinks-plenty of favors to chose from which is always a plus! But nothing crazy to write home about.

Atmosphere and ambiance are above many. Credit where it is due. 

However a major downside is that their outside area is not dog friendly. I actually pulled up with my dog the first time and had to leave. Only went at a later date bc it was someone's going away brunch and I kinda had to. 

There are SO MANY OTHER dog friendly places (again-why aren't they allowed in the outside dining? Weird)
I'll be giving every other pup friendly place in the city my business instead. 

I advise you to as well. (Nemi and cantina are personal faves)

Not dog friendly. Pretty sad that they are so behind with the rest of the brewery scene. EVEN when there is outside seating. Makes no sense that the tiny gate defining the outdoor space and the sidewalk where pets walk by makes much of a difference to the dept of health..

No dogs allowed. Pretty pathetic to have false information on the yelp page of such a popular establishment. Nothing like relying on false information here and planning a visit with friends only to not be let in. Trash

Came here with a friend a few weeks ago. I had my dog with me so we were looking for an outdoor bar or cafe on our way back to rittenhouse from penn's landing. Wasn't sure if dogs were allowed, but we walk in and a waiter greets us and bends down to pet the dog. We keep walking, and a busboy stops to coo at the dog.  We continue on to the bar and another waiter waves and says "aww your dog is so cute." ok, so...all signs point to "dogs are welcome here." We stop at the bar and I think i spot one of my favorite beers on tap. I ask the bartender if that is indeed kona big wave that I see and he stares at me blankly and then slowly nods his head. Ok, i think to myself, this dude obviously has some developmental challenges. No judgement. I will keep that in mind.  After staring at me and my friend aggressively for a good minute, he says "dogs are not allowed on the premise, im not even kidding. im serious. im totally serious. you cant have a dog anywhere on the property. im dead serious."   The weird part was that I wasn't protesting or challenging him, i was nodding my head and picking up my bag to leave. Again, i thought he had some mental health issues and I didnt want to be rude. But as we left, we noticed that he morphed into a smiling affable bartender with the white customers who had been seated next to us.  I mean I know its really brain busting work to be a bartender (its practically rocket science compared to my doctorate degree in neuroscience....), but still dude...are you THAT dumb? Racist scumbag. 

In any case, this place was a dark alleyway between two drab office buildings on market street.   We were happy to leave and found a much better place a few blocks up.

Stumbling upon this restaurant at the corner of passyunk Ave was an interesting experience to say the least. 

We began with fruity and strong margaritas, which preceded two appetizers that were a mixed bag. The ceviche had a fresh selection of fish, although the lack of lime allowed the spices to overpower the flavor. The nachos were too heavy. The beef itself was tasty, but it's amount was excessive on the dish and it overwhelmed the nachos themselves. The chicken enchiladas consistency was mushy and the tomatillo sauce didn't provide an exciting balance. The Korean short rib tacos was a tasty cut of meat that should have been enjoyed on its own. It felt out of place on the poorly proportioned taco, and the lack of chemistry with the ingredients was a turnoff. 

Overall the food was average, but disappointingly the service did not exceed this mark either. Our waiter rarely passed our table, and due to a miscommunication we ordered appetizers but not our entrees for quite a long time. I really appreciate them being dog friendly while we ate outside, but I do not think I'll be returning here anytime soon.

Green eggs is great. Food has always been phenomenal. The only thing really hasn't been up to par is their customer service. As usual, every time we go to green eggs, we always call to see how  long the wait is - specially for Sunday brunch. This time, we had our dog so before walking all the way to this location, I wanted to be sure that they are dog friendly with their outdoor seating. The hostess told me yes. After walking 45 minutes to this location, the hostess was extremely rude and was not accommodating at all. She said that she didn't know who I spoke to but they do not accept animals even if we sit outside. As a person in the restaurant industry, we understand but the attitude from the staff was certainly not needed.

Decent coffee, but the staff really kills this place. Emotionless, rude, and unwelcoming. This place is just a block from home so I've tried many times to enjoy it but alas I'm giving up. It's also no longer dog friendly despite previously allowing pups for years.

I stayed here for a weekend and I do not think I would stay here again. The positives this hotel has going for it are its location ( a couple of blocks away from the wonderful Reading Central Terminal, Independence hall, and shopping) and the rooms are nicely appointed. The rooms look recently redone with flat screen televisions and attractive marble bathrooms. Also, each room has a Keureg coffeemaker with delicious complimentary coffee as well as an empty refrigerator. That should make for a nice stay however, the negatives are as follows: 

1) There are no king-sized beds in the hotel although there is certainly room for them. No big deal but would be nice. 

2) I requested a wake up call and it was never made- this is totally unacceptable. 

3) My room was not made up even though I was out of it at 9:00am. At 5:30 pm, the housekeeper finally knocked on my door and asked if I just wanted towels which made me think she wanted to avoid cleaning the room, but I told her, no I want the room cleaned which was eventually done. I found this very unprofessional. 

4) This hotel is pet friendly and although they confine pets to one floor I witnessed a dog defecate in the lobby, not far from their fish restaurant. That was pretty gross. 

5) The comforter on the bed was entirely too warm for summer, and the extra blanket in the room was a twin, only useful for one person. 

6) There was no iron in the room which is often useful for travelers. 

I don't know if I was there on a very busy weekend or what, but despite the nice room and good location, the above problems make it doubtful I would return to this hotel.

你正在为餐饮评论召回系统建立逆向评测集。输入是同一个固定特征下的一批真实 Yelp 完整评论。

当前固定特征：pet_friendly
中文含义：从不允许宠物到非常宠物友好
用户希望的方向：higher
满足要求的英文含义：["Dogs and other pets are welcome and treated well at the restaurant.", "The restaurant provides a pet-friendly space or amenities for dogs."]
违反要求的英文含义：["Dogs or pets are not allowed and the restaurant is not pet friendly.", "Customers are refused service or seating because they brought a pet."]

请从输入评论中恰好选择4条：2条明确满足要求，expected_direction=positive；2条明确违反要求，expected_direction=negative。每条评论最多使用一次。

要求：

1. query_text 必须是自然的中文找餐馆问题，只表达当前固定特征和指定方向。
2. query_text 不得出现商家名称、评论编号，也不得暗示已经知道答案。
3. requirement_text 用简短中文写清需要评论回答的要求。
4. evidence_span 必须逐字复制 review_text 中一段连续原文；不能翻译、改写、拼接或补字。
5. 原文必须能够直接证明正面或反面。泛泛的总体好评、差评、星级倾向和意思不清楚的句子不能使用。
6. 如果评论只提到相邻概念但不能证明当前特征，不要选择。
7. 4条样本的问题可以换自然说法，但不能改变指定特征和用户希望的方向。
8. 证据必须直接说明商家确实满足或违反要求。仅仅说“A比B更好/更差”、假设以后会怎样、或者只有在某个未满足条件下才成立，都不能当作明确证据。
9. 只返回下面这一种JSON结构，不要增加字段，不要返回Markdown代码块，不要解释：

{
  "drafts": [
    {
      "seed_review_id": "必须来自候选的review_id",
      "query_text": "自然中文问题",
      "requirement_text": "简短中文要求",
      "expected_direction": "positive或negative",
      "evidence_span": "从对应review_text逐字复制的连续原文"
    }
  ]
}

drafts必须恰好有4项，且必须是2项positive和2项negative。
